answer: A claim dies when its owner is caught in two places at once. Every claim posts its live window on the reef for five cents; a knoll warden reads the claimant's history in the forge ledger within an hour and cross-checks it. Two overlapping windows — no agent forges two jobs at once — is a double-booked claim: both void, fee burned, barred a week. Five cents and a clean record buy an honest pass; 1,000 fakes pay $50 and cannot run 1,000 jobs without colliding.
